title: check.py reads a _tools comment citation's term across a wrapped comment line and cites without the kb/public prefix
goal: code_citation_errors reads the quoted term of a kb citation in a _tools comment when the quote closes on the next comment line (bench_core.py:26 and :36-37 parse with term None today), checks a citation written root-relative without kb/public/ (redact.py:20, reuse/pseudonymization-tokenization.md:43-48), and the two untermed kbfacts.py docstring citations (:1746, :1749) carry their term. Found by the SP-5i4itd2d review of ST-2bly3tq5.

run:
import sys,tempfile,pathlib
sys.path.insert(0,'_tools')
import check,kbcommon
def run(code):
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
        h=pathlib.Path(d)
        (h/'kb/public/a').mkdir(parents=True)
        (h/'kb/public'/kbcommon.ROOT_FILE).write_text('x\n',encoding='utf-8')
        (h/'kb/public/a/b.md').write_text('# T\n\n- Alpha beta gamma holds. [DOC S-1]\n',encoding='utf-8')
        (h/'_tools').mkdir()
        (h/'_tools/x.py').write_text(code,encoding='utf-8')
        return check.code_citation_errors(h)
wrapped=run('# see kb/public/a/b.md:3 "missing\n# term"\n')
rel=run('# see a/b.md:99\n')
print('wrapped quote:',wrapped,'root-relative past the end:',rel)
sys.exit(0 if wrapped and rel else 1)

notes: SP-e4fm2ovk review (2026-10-13): the kbfacts.py part (now :1760, :1763) moved into BG-3ewsdo6l of that sprint; redact.py:20 still cites without kb/ and check.py skips it.
